issues.legal_issue: A High Court deciding a second appeal must formulate substantial questions of law before finally deciding the appeal and may not first formulate them in its final judgment.
material_facts: The High Court allowed a second appeal and dismissed the underlying suit.
The High Court did not formulate any substantial question of law when admitting the second appeal, but first framed two questions in its final judgment and answered them.
The High Court did not use the procedure for framing an additional substantial question of law at the final hearing by assigning reasons.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s procedure did not comply with the mandatory requirements governing second appeals and amounted to a jurisdictional error. Its judgment was set aside, and the case was remanded for the High Court to decide the second appeal afresh after hearing the appellant and formulating any substantial questions of law that arise.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100(1), (3), (4) and (5) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a second appeal can be decided only if it involves a substantial question of law; the High Court must formulate that question, and the appeal must be heard on the question formulated. The proviso to Section 100(5) permits an additional substantial question at the hearing only if the High Court records reasons for framing it. These requirements are mandatory, and the High Court’s jurisdiction to decide the appeal finally depends on following them. The Court relied on Surat Singh (Dead) v. Siri Bhagwan & Ors., (2018) 4 SCC 562, including its discussion of Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari (Deceased) by L.Rs., (2001) 3 SCC 179, and on the principle that when a statute prescribes a manner for doing an act, it must be done in that manner, as stated in Baru Ram v. Parsanni (Smt.), AIR 1959 SC 93.

predicates.second_appeal: The court was deciding an appeal to a High Court from a decree passed by a subordinate court in appeal.
predicates.questions_first_formulated_in_final_judg: The High Court first formulated the substantial questions of law in its final judgment instead of formulating them before finally deciding the appeal.

issues.definition: When a High Court deciding a second appeal first formulates the substantial questions of law in its final judgment, the judgment is set aside and the case is remanded for a fresh decision.
